meta-governance as applied in the Randstad is effective in creating a strategic framework for the implementation of central government investments in the region, but that it is limited in its ability to create a truly integrated strategy.

meta-governance, as we define it, is a useful concept in understanding how governance processes can be coordinated, integrated and made coherent in fragmented governance structures.
meta-governance as an analytical tool is useful for the Randstad case and for other regional cases where governance arrangements stumble upon each other.
meta-governance can be effective, but only in a context of a strong institutional framework and in a setting where the involved stakeholders have a common interest and a common goal.
